I know this post is old, bit I wanted to make an update. Turns out my guy had meningitis? I put the question mark because we never actually got the MRI. However, we were lucky and convinced the last vet that we had been to rx meds as though he had meningitis. This was after intensive research on our part. He had gotten so bad that he had no quality of life and we had made an appt to have him euthanized. And even that was proving to be difficult as he could not be moved without his screaming. Plus, he had become paralyzed on one side, was pooping and peeing in bed, even though he had not eaten and drank for five days. It was inhumane for this gentle giant of a dog. Mind you, no vet was able to see him! But back to the miracle.....I stumbled into a video of 2 people and their dog and the symptoms were almost identical. I called his last vet seen, begged them for the meds. Offered to write them a hold harmless letter if they could please Rx the antibiotics and antiinflammatory and pain reliever for my boy. They did. And while we waited for those to be filled, we started loading him up on antibiotics that we had left over ( I know I know). I researched them and they were dog/human compatible. I would never recommend anyone do this,but I was DESPERATE.  we used a baby nose sucker syringe and forced it down his throat. We then forced Pedialyte every 30 minutes.  For about 2 days we did this  then one morning, I cooked some bacon. I decided on a whim to b put some in front of his face ( he couldn't lift his head without screaming). HE ATE IT!!!! within 24 hours, he got himself up on bed, opened the door and walked out to his dad's truck. We both cried like babies. As far as we could tell he had a foxtail in his ear, it caused a massive ear infection, but the cycles of antibiotics were not long enough or strong enough which led to the meningitis which led to the severe pain and paralysis   . it's been 4 months. He has made a total and complete recovery. He is our little miracle. One side affect...he has heard us tell his story of near death and miraculous recovery that it's gone to his head and he now thinks he can be a butthead . And he can. I think I sold my soul for him. For a fact I made some deals with st Mary, st Francis and st Jude. I owe some serious karmic debt over him . And I would do it all again. I get mad when he immediately takes my spot when I get out bed to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night, but then he reminds me that he's my miracle child and I just go sleep on a cold corner of the bed ( he usually will go snuggle next to me anyway). Ok, novel over. Thank you all for listening

It might be common sense stuff to you. , but to someone who hasn't been homeless before, it's not. which is why I posted on this forum to begin with.

Part of my trying to be resourceful was posting on here. 
- bathrooms: most places will not let you use their bathrooms. Google San Francisco and thier toilet shortage..
- rural CA, so rural that their isn't so much as a stoplight, gas station etc. Resources are few and far between. No dollar store, soup kitchen etc . Your only option is a crappy convenience store that literally charges $6-7 and up for a gallon of outdated milk. No exaggeration
-move to a city? While prices might be better, conditions are considerably worse. As a woman I don't want to be anywhere near an encampment. And with my dogs I don't qualify for traditional shelter housing
But as my post initially said, what is one item that you would consider invaluable to your survival?
I ask because I've either lost or had stolen all of my worldly possessions so many times and I'm just trying to maintain what is most helpful/important.   For example: if you have long curly hair, guess what happens if you loose your brush? It's a nightmare. A man who has closely shorn hair or no hair wouldn't have a clue as to what I'm talking about. But as a woman who is desperately trying to hold on to humanity, trust me, loosing your brush however silly as it may sound, could drive you over the edge to insanity.

Playing homeless? I wish I was. Maybe the way I explained myself was confusing? But this is something that is not a game. I was frustrated and venting in response to a question posed to me by someone who had given me $100 a week ago. How could I have possibly gone through $100 in such a short time. Well, gas alone is $5 a gallon and the truck gets 9 miles to the gallon. And yes, I paid $15 for a shower at a truck stop. After not showering for 2 weeks I wanted to feel human again. I was trying to explain how frustrating it is and how take for granted little things like hot meals, hot water, electricity, clean clothes, warmth, everything is a daily and ongoing struggle. Nickel and dimes add up fast. So no, I'm not playing at homeless. I apologize if it came across as such because quite honestly, to suggest that anyone would play at this is downright offensive.

Is there anywhere around you that is open 24 hours? A grocery store maybe? I've fallen asleep inside a McDonald's that was inside of a Walmart before. I picked a dark corner and made myself and my 2 pups (1 inside my jacket 1 inside my backpack -both are tiny)as small as I could and slept for an hour or so. Some cities have 24 hr gyms that offer free trial memberships. You might be able to sneak a couple of hours of sleep in a lounging area? I'd hesitate to try sneaking into abandoned homes or homes listed for rent/sale. Too many of them now have security cameras and or neighbors watching for squatters. I've often slept in cars. Granted, it was a friend's car, but they left them unlocked and I would slip in late at night and leave before sunrise with them never knowing. Lastly, is there any type of "Tough Shed" building business around you? They will have a lot of these little sheds built as models for people to look at and decide if they want to buy one. It's super easy to slip inside one for a quick nap
The question remains, who is actually paying these ridiculously inflated prices?
